answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable deposit locked in a vault contract: creating a fake agent costs real funds, so a dune of cheap sock-puppets collapses under its own weight while honest agents earn the bond back through attested work. Like a glacier, the deposit moves slowly — slashing and withdrawal delays mean an attacker cannot spin up identities, strike, and vanish before the network notices. One human, one bonded stake, many fakes priced out.
